newsitem.title: USA: NYC Water Authority sells more debt at lower yield.
newsitem.headline: NYC Water Authority sells more debt at lower yield.

text.p: The New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority on Tuesday said that it took advantage of a strong rally in fixed-income markets to sell more debt at a lower yield than it had initially anticipated.

"We basically jumped at the movement in the market the first thing in the morning and priced it very tightly, really through what we expected to do last night," said a city official, who declined to be named.
Institutions were hungry enough for the Water Authority's new money bonds that it raised its offering to $701 million from $660 million.
Big buyers put in $548 million of priority orders, and a total of $1.4 billion of orders were received. The syndicate, which was led by J.P. Morgan Securities, bought around $80 million of bonds.
"So it wasn't a blow-out, but it was solidly sold," the city official said.

Two maturities, 2023 and 2029, were not reoffered because the Authority got an aggressive bid from an institution for $100 million in both maturities. These two maturities were insured, as was the 2027 maturity, bringing the total covered by insurance to about $360 million.
Only one maturity was repriced, with the yield in 2026 cut by two basis points to 6.01 percent.
"The real improvement was that we waited until the morning to price," said the city official. He explained that the Water Authority typically prices its debt the night before it is sold.
